description: Sync messages and thread replies from the Slack channels you choose, with private channels limited to their members.
intro: The Slack connector reads the public and private channels you select in one Slack workspace. Each message becomes one document, and each thread reply is its own document linked to the message that started the thread.
Files shared in a message are downloaded and read with it. A private channel's messages can be limited to the channel's members.

connect.auth: Slack uses a token from a Slack app installed in your workspace. A bot token or a user token works.

credentials.name: access_token
credentials.text: A Slack bot token, which starts with `xoxb-`, or a user token, which starts with `xoxp-`.

connect.permissions_label: Scopes to add to the Slack app

permissions.name: channels:read
permissions.text: lists public channels in the channel picker.

permissions.name: groups:read
permissions.text: lists private channels in the channel picker.

permissions.name: users:read.email
permissions.text: without it, permissions cannot be captured for any private channel.

connect.permissions_note: If neither `channels:read` nor `groups:read` is granted, connecting fails with a message that names the missing scope.

steps.title: Create a Slack app
steps.text: Create a Slack app for your workspace and add the scopes above.

steps.title: Install it
steps.text: Install the app in the workspace and copy its token.

steps.title: Select channels
steps.text: Discover lists every public and private channel that is not archived and that the token can see, with whether it is private, whether the app is a member, and its member count. Select the channels to sync.

connect.account: One token covers one Slack workspace.

documents.name: Messages
documents.one_document: One Slack message: a message posted in a channel, or a single reply in a thread.
documents.title: The channel name with `#`, a colon and the message's first line, cut to about 80 characters, for example `#general: Deploy is done`. A reply reads `#general thread: ...`. A message with no text is titled `Slack message`.
documents.text: The message text, with mentions turned into display names. Then the pretext, title and text of any legacy attachments, and one `[file: name]` line per shared file. The sender is written as a `From` line and the time as a `Sent` line.
documents.link_back: A Slack permalink to the message. A reply links to itself inside its thread. Empty if the workspace address could not be read.
documents.files: Each shared file is downloaded and read, and its text becomes searchable with the message. A file is skipped if Slack gave no download address, the download fails, or the file is too large.

attributes.name: Message text
attributes.text: The text described above. This is what a query matches, and what HydraDB reads for people and topics.

attributes.name: author
purposes: Person or group in the graph
attributes.text: The display name of the person or bot that posted, or the raw Slack id if the name could not be read. It is the `From` line, and the graph records the message as sent by that person.

attributes.name: Shared files
attributes.text: The text read from each shared file, searchable with the message.

attributes.name: title
attributes.text: Labels the message with its channel and opening words in results. When the message has text, search matches the message itself, so the channel name in the title is not guaranteed to match a query.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: The message time. It is the document date used for recency, and the `Sent` line of the text.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.slack_ts
attributes.text: The message's Slack timestamp. Picks out one exact message.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.slack_thread_ts
attributes.text: The timestamp of the thread's first message, empty outside a thread. Limits a query to one thread.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.slack_subtype
attributes.text: Slack's message subtype, such as `bot_message` or `file_share`. Includes or excludes bot posts and file shares.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.slack_bot_id
attributes.text: The bot id when a bot posted the message. Includes or excludes one bot's messages.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.slack_reply_count
attributes.text: How many replies the thread has. Finds thread starters by how many replies they drew.

attributes.name: connector_id
attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector. Access rules you set on a channel are matched to messages through it.

attributes.name: provider
attributes.text: Always `slack`.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: For a reply, the message that started its thread. Joins the reply to that message, so the whole conversation can be returned together.

attributes.name: thread_id
attributes.text: The thread a message belongs to. Groups every message of one thread together in the graph.

attributes.name: mentions
purposes: Person or group in the graph
attributes.text: Display names of people mentioned in the message. The graph records each as mentioned. The names are searchable as part of the message text.

attributes.name: Channel
attributes.text: The selected channel. For a private channel, its members decide who can read its messages.

attributes.name: attachment_count
attributes.text: How many legacy attachments the message had.

attributes.name: file_count
attributes.text: How many shared files Slack listed, including any that could not be downloaded.

attributes.name: is_edited
attributes.text: Whether Slack marked the message as edited when it was read. Later edits are not picked up automatically.

attributes.name: edited_by
attributes.text: The display name of the editor, when edited. The editor is not added to the graph as a person.

attributes.name: edited_at
attributes.text: The edit time, when edited. The document date stays the original message time.

attributes.name: slack_files
attributes.text: The details Slack supplied for each shared file, kept even when a file's text could not be read.

attributes.name: Reactions
attributes.text: Reactions are not read.

connections: A thread reply to the message that started the thread.
Every message to its thread, including a message nobody replied to.
No links to items in other tools.
people: An editor is kept with the message but not added to the graph.
graph.from_text: Topics, decisions, people and organisations named in prose, in the message text, legacy attachment text and shared file text. Each reply is read together with the text of its thread's first message.

permissions.who_can_read: A public channel's messages can be read by the whole workspace. A private channel's messages can be read by its members. HydraDB reads this once per channel on each sync; there is no per-message permission.
permissions.identity: A member's email address, in lower case. Bots and deactivated users have no email and are left out.
permissions.when_unreadable: If HydraDB cannot read a channel's privacy, members or member emails, an access rule you set on that channel stays in force. Without a rule, the connector status shows a permission warning, and depending on your deployment's setting the messages either stay readable or are hidden until permissions can be read.
notes: A private channel with more than 1,000 members who have emails, or more than 3,000 members in all, cannot be captured. Set an access rule on such a channel.
Without `users:read.email`, permissions cannot be captured for any private channel.

sync.first_sync: A newly selected channel reads back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default.
sync.changes: Each sync reads recent history for new messages, and new replies on threads whose latest reply moved. A second pass, every 6 hours by default, walks the channel's whole history in steps to find new replies on older threads.
sync.edits: A routine sync does not pick up an edit to a message that is already indexed.
sync.deletes: Deleted messages are not removed. A message deleted in Slack stays searchable in HydraDB.

not_synced: Archived channels: discovery does not offer them.
Direct messages and group direct messages.
System messages: joins, leaves, renames, topic and purpose changes, pins, bots being added or removed, and thread broadcasts.
Edits and deletions made after a message was indexed.
questions: What did the team decide about the release last week?
What did Priya say in the thread about the pricing change?
Which messages were posted by the alerts bot?
What does the PDF shared in the design channel say about the new layout?

good_to_know.title: Naming a channel does not filter to it.
good_to_know.text: When a message has text, search matches the message, not its `#channel` title. A channel name in a query does not reliably limit results to that channel.

good_to_know.title: A name that could not be read stays an id.
good_to_know.text: If HydraDB could not read a person's name, the message keeps the raw Slack id, and later syncs do not go back to fix it.
